interview.hardest_part: Accurately cross-checking the growing set of late-game documents and story-specific instructions while the workday clock runs, using precise one-action-at-a-time mouse input. Reaching day 29 quickly enough and then satisfying a specific success-ending path is substantially harder than surviving the early days.
interview.likely_failure: A slow or incorrect inspection sequence will cause citations, lost income, and too few processed entrants; this can compound into family deaths, arrest, or another premature ending. I am most likely to stall around the middle workdays as document requirements multiply, or run out of the three-hour budget before reaching a qualifying ending.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Progress is saved by native workday, early rules are comparatively simple, documents and the rulebook expose most required information visually, and obvious discrepancies allow fast denials. Time between workdays permits careful review of new rules, and routine cases can be handled with repeated interface patterns.
interview.harmful_mechanics: The clock continues during deliberation, crowded documents require accurate dragging and stamping, and each screenshot permits only one mouse action. Later days add overlapping checks and exceptions, while citations, low pay, family expenses, scripted incidents, and irreversible story choices can end the single attempt. The three-hour cap also makes reaching day 29 and a specific approved ending difficult.
